title: Variables and functions
reflection: In the pyramid, the function square(side) did three different jobs. How many lines did it save you? What else could you build with it?

steps.goal: MINE has built a wall in front of Byte, at a distance you don't know. Write a program that takes Byte up to the wall and makes it say how many steps it took.
steps.not_yet: Not yet: Byte has to stop right in front of the wall and say how many steps it took.
hints: A variable remembers a number: local steps = 0 at the start, then steps = steps + 1 every time Byte moves forward.
Walk with while not byte.detect() do ... end, as in the conditions lesson. At the end: mine.say("I took " .. steps .. " steps").
block_hints: In Variables, create a variable steps: "set steps to 0" at the start, then "change steps by 1" every time Byte moves forward.
Walk with "repeat while" and "not block in front?" in it, as in the conditions lesson. At the end use "say" with "create text with" in it: "I took ", steps, " steps".

steps.goal: Each time your program starts, MINE chooses how big a square it wants: local side = mine.challenge() tells you. Build a solid square floor of that size.
steps.block_goal: Each time your program starts, MINE chooses how big a square it wants: the challenge's number block tells you. Build a solid square floor of that size.
steps.not_yet: Not yet: build a solid square floor as big as mine.challenge() asks.
hints: It's the floor of the loops lesson, with side instead of the numbers: for row = 1, side do ... end and for i = 1, side do ... end.
To see what MINE asks, make Byte say it: mine.say("Side: " .. side).
block_hints: It's the floor of the loops lesson: "set side to" with "the challenge's number" in it, then put side in every "repeat" instead of the numbers.
To see what MINE asks, make Byte say it: "say" with "create text with" "Side: " and side in it.

steps.goal: Build a step pyramid: a 5 × 5 square, a 3 × 3 square on top of it, and one block on the very top. Write a function square(side) and use it three times.
steps.block_goal: Build a step pyramid: a 5 × 5 square, a 3 × 3 square on top of it, and one block on the very top. Make a function square with a parameter side, and use it three times.
steps.not_yet: Not yet: the pyramid is a solid 5 × 5 square, then a 3 × 3 square centred on top of it, then one block on top: 35 blocks.
hints: function square(side) ... end gives a name to your square program: then square(5), square(3) and square(1) build the three layers. Make the function bring Byte back to the corner where it started.
Between two layers: go up one block, move forward one, turn right, move forward one and turn left. Then the next square is centred.
block_hints: In Functions, take "to do something" and call it square; with ⚙ add an input side. Put your square inside: then "square with side" 5, 3 and 1 builds the three layers. Make it bring Byte back to the corner where it started.
Between two layers: "move up", "move forward", "turn right", "move forward", "turn left". Then the next square is centred.
